_about: The wager, the goods, and the words the game says when something happens. What decides each event is in renderer/game.js, beside the event's id; the words and the chapter are here, so they can be checked against the novel without reading code.

wager.terms: Twenty thousand pounds, laid at the Reform Club, that the circuit of the world can be made in eighty days: back in this room by a quarter before nine in the evening of Saturday, the 21st of December, 1872.
wager.dateLine: Travelling eastward, Fogg sees the sun cross the meridian eighty times while London counts seventy-nine days. So once the circuit crosses the Pacific eastward, his diary runs one day ahead of London's calendar, and the wager is judged by London's.

goods.label: Fur coats
goods.why: The sledge crosses the prairie in hard frost.

goods.label: Lumps of sugar
goods.use: Give Kiouni a lump of sugar

club.newspaper: Ralph, a director of the Bank of England, talks of the robbery three days ago: fifty-five thousand pounds, taken by a gentleman. Detectives have been sent to every principal port.
club.whist: Fogg plays a rubber of whist with Stuart, Fallentin, Sullivan, Flanagan and Ralph.

suez-detective.diary: A detective on the quay compares Fogg's face with the description of the bank robber.

suez-servant-visa.diary: Passepartout takes the passport to the consulate and tells a friendly stranger everything about the wager.

suez-own-visa.diary: Fogg has the passport stamped himself, and says nothing to anyone.

bombay-temple.diary: Passepartout wanders into the pagoda on Malabar Hill in his shoes, and is thrown out by the priests.

calcutta-court.diary: Fogg and Passepartout are arrested at the station for the affair of the pagoda. Bail is a thousand pounds each.

kholby-end.diary: The railway stops in a glade at Kholby. Fifty miles to Allahabad were never laid.

kiouni-bought.diary: At two thousand pounds the owner yields, and Kiouni is Fogg's.

pillaji-procession.diary: Through the trees a procession passes, bearing a young widow to be burned at dawn.

pillaji-rescue.diary: At dawn the widow is carried off from the pyre. Her name is Aouda.

pillaji-no-guide.diary: Without the Parsee guide nobody can find a way to the pagoda through the dark.

hongkong-tavern.diary: Passepartout drinks with a stranger in a tavern, is drugged with opium, and never tells Fogg that the Carnatic sails tonight.

hongkong-missed.diary: The Carnatic has sailed without Fogg. Passepartout is aboard her, alone.

yokohama-circus.diary: In the middle of the Long Noses' human pyramid Passepartout sees his master, and the pyramid collapses.

fortkearney-attack.diary: The train is attacked near Fort Kearney. Passepartout is carried off, and the train goes on without its passengers.

fortkearney-rescue.diary: Fogg leads soldiers of the fort after the war party and brings Passepartout back.

sledge-cold.diary: Without fur coats the cold is cruel, and the sledge stops twice to thaw its passengers.

henrietta-burned.diary: The coal is gone. Fogg buys the Henrietta for sixty thousand dollars, and burns her upper works to reach Ireland.

henrietta-drifts.diary: The coal is gone and the carpet-bag cannot buy the ship. The Henrietta crawls under sail.

liverpool-warrant.diary: On the Liverpool quay the Detective lays his hand on Fogg's shoulder and serves his warrant.

liverpool-free.diary: The real robber was arrested on the 17th of December, in Edinburgh. Fogg is free.

liverpool-no-warrant.diary: The Detective's warrant never catches up with Fogg.

london-late.diary: By Fogg's diary it is five minutes too late. He believes the wager is lost.

london-dateline.diary: It is not Saturday but Friday. Travelling east, Fogg gained a day, and London's calendar is a day behind his diary.

won.diary: Fogg walks into the saloon of the Reform Club. "Here I am, gentlemen."

lost-late.diary: The eighty days have run out. The wager is lost.

lost-funds.diary: The carpet-bag cannot pay for any way on. Fogg is without funds.
